arguments.summary: APT alert triggered on host 10.0.9.50 (WS-IT-101), a low-criticality IT workstation. Initial containment steps were misaligned with actual risk, proposing destructive actions (e.g., disabling real-time AV, Sysmon logging). Post-analysis revealed no active compromise: network scans from external IP were blocked, user behavior was benign, and files analyzed were clean. A false positive occurred due to misattribution of external scan activity. The proposed containment plan was dangerously excessive for the asset and risk level. Corrective actions included blocking the source IP (10.0.5.14), performing a full AV scan (which detected a file later determined to be a false positive), and revoking unnecessary privileges from the svc_forensic_tool account, which should not have existed on this endpoint.

Admin phase: Source IP 10.0.5.14 blocked. Full AV scan run (false positive detected). Privileges for svc_forensic_tool revoked.
Incident reclassified as false positive. Root cause: alert logic misfired on benign scan artifact and triggered an over-aggressive, template-based response.
